rules.title: Method lookup on a primitive receiver tries value, &T, &mut T, *const T, *mut T in order
rules.statement: For a method call `recv.method(args)` where `recv`'s type is a primitive (mangled key `<type>__<method>`), resolution tries param[0] = `T` (value), then `&T`, then `&mut T`, then `*const T`, then `*mut T`, accepting the first exact-signature match. This exposes `impl Trait for T` methods declared with `self: &Self`/`&mut Self`/`self: *const Self`/`self: *mut Self` to dot-call on a bare-value receiver.

rules.title: `impl Trait for &T` / `&mut T` (T non-struct) registers under `$ref_`/`$mut_ref_` mangled keys
rules.statement: When `recv`'s type is `&T`/`&mut T` and no bare-`T` impl matched, method lookup additionally tries the mangled key `$ref_<T>__<method>` (or `$mut_ref_` for `&mut T`), first with `recv`'s type as param[0] as-is, then with an added `&`/`&mut` level (for `self: &Self` methods whose Self is already `&T`). On match, `recv` is auto-ref'd to the matching level via `materialize_recv_ref`.

rules.title: Generic blanket impl `impl<T> Trait for &T` dispatches via sentinel key with T bound to the pointee
rules.statement: When `recv`'s type is `&T`/`&mut T` and no concrete `$ref_`-mangled impl matched, lookup tries the generic sentinel key `$ref_$T__<method>` / `$mut_ref_$T__<method>`. On match, the impl's type parameter named `T` is bound to `recv`'s pointee type, other type params bind to an error placeholder, `recv` is auto-ref'd (`&recv`), and the call routes through `finish_generic_call` for monomorphization.

rules.title: `&T`/`&mut T` receiver auto-derefs to T's method when no ref-targeted impl is found
rules.statement: For a primitive-or-ref receiver of type `&T`/`&mut T`, if no `T`-value, `&T`-impl, or generic `&T`-blanket impl matched, resolution derefs to the pointee type `T` and retries lookup under `<T>__<method>` with param[0] = `T`; if that also fails, it retries with param[0] left as the original ref type (covers a `self: &Self` method reached only via this path). The receiver expression is rebuilt via an explicit deref only in the pointee-param[0] case.

rules.title: A `&mut T` receiver may satisfy a `&self` method on T by demoting to `&T`
rules.statement: If auto-deref lookup for a `&mut T` receiver fails to find a `T`-value method, resolution retries once more with param[0] coerced to `&T` (demoted mutability, same pointee) before falling back to a generic-function lookup under the same mangled key.

rules.title: Calling an unsafe method requires an unsafe context
rules.statement: A method-call resolved to a function-info marked `is_unsafe` is rejected unless the call site is lexically inside an `unsafe` block/context.

rules.title: Method-call turbofish type args are used verbatim, padded with an error type if short
rules.statement: For a generic method call with explicit turbofish (`x.foo::<A,B>()`), the supplied type arguments are bound positionally to the method's type parameters without inference; any type parameter beyond the supplied count binds to the error type.

rules.title: Generic-method type-argument inference seeds `Self` from the receiver's type
rules.statement: When a generic method call has no turbofish, type-argument inference runs over the argument expressions with the substitution seeded `Self := (receiver's type)`, starting from parameter index 1 (the receiver itself is excluded from the inferred-from set). Failure to infer all type parameters is a diagnostic.

rules.title: Method call auto-refs the receiver when the resolved method expects `&Self`/`&mut Self`
rules.statement: If the resolved method's formal parameter 0 is `&Self`/`&mut Self` and the receiver expression's type is not already ref-like or a raw pointer, the receiver is implicitly wrapped in `&`/`&mut` (materialized as an address-of-temp) to match, matching the formal's mutability.

rules.title: Method call auto-addresses the receiver when the resolved method expects `*const Self`/`*mut Self`
rules.statement: If the resolved method's formal parameter 0 is a raw pointer type (`*const Self`/`*mut Self`) and the receiver's type is neither ref-like nor already a pointer, the receiver is implicitly wrapped in the matching raw-pointer form.

rules.title: Value blanket impl (`impl<T> Trait for T`) is tried as a last resort for primitive receivers
rules.statement: If no method-info was resolved for a primitive receiver through any of the concrete/ref/generic lookup paths, dispatch falls back to the generic value-blanket-impl mechanism before reporting an error.

rules.title: Method call on a non-struct receiver with no resolvable method is a diagnostic
rules.statement: If a method-call receiver is a primitive/ref/pointer type and no method-info is found through any lookup path (direct, ref-mangled, generic, deref, blanket), sema reports "method call: receiver is not a struct (got <type>)" — suppressed only when in metaprog-discovery mode and the receiver (or, for ref/ptr receivers, its pointee) is already the error type, to avoid cascading diagnostics.

rules.title: `str` receivers fall back to `Slice<u8>`-typed method lookup under the `str__` mangling
rules.statement: `str` is represented as `&[u8]` (`type_str` yields `&[u8]`), but impls written `impl Trait for str` register methods mangled as `str__<method>`. When receiver type-string is `&[u8]` and lookup under the literal `&[u8]__<method>` key fails, resolution retries under `str__<method>` (concrete, then generic).

rules.title: Struct-receiver ref-typed impls (`$ref_`/`$mut_ref_`) are tried before auto-deref'd bare-type impls
rules.statement: When a struct-typed receiver's expression type is `&T`/`&mut T`, method lookup first tries mangled keys `$ref_<T>__<method>` (and, if T is a generic struct instantiation, also its base-name form) or `$mut_ref_<T>__<method>`, against the receiver's type as-is, then `&recv`, then `&mut recv` as param[0] (in that order), before falling through to the bare-`T` auto-deref path below. This lets `impl Trait for &T` win over an auto-deref'd `impl Trait for T`.

rules.title: A generic ref-impl's type parameters bind from the pointee struct's own type-argument list
rules.statement: For a matched `$ref_`/`$mut_ref_`-mangled method belonging to a generic impl, the impl's type parameters are bound positionally to the receiver pointee struct's type-argument list (looked up by struct/datatype name), and the call routes through `finish_generic_call`; for a non-generic matched method, the same substitution is applied to compute the concrete return type.

rules.title: Struct-method candidate selection matches receiver/args against each candidate's formal signature with one autoref/autoderef step
rules.statement: Among same-name non-generic candidates with matching arity, a candidate matches if: (a) receiver type equals formal param[0] exactly, OR (b) formal param[0] is `&T`/`&mut T`/`*T` and actual receiver's type equals its pointee (autoref/auto-addr the receiver to match), OR (c) both are raw pointers with equal pointee (const/mut pointer receivers are mutually compatible), OR (d) actual receiver is `&T`/`&mut T`/`*T` and formal param[0] is the bare pointee type (auto-deref candidate, by-value self) — otherwise the general `types_compatible` check applies; AND every remaining argument is `arg_compatible_for_dispatch` against its formal (with struct type-param substitution applied to formals when the receiver is a generic struct instantiation).

rules.title: An auto-deref'd by-value-`self` candidate is chosen only when no non-deref candidate matches
rules.statement: A candidate reachable only by auto-dereffing the receiver to satisfy a by-value `self` parameter is recorded but not immediately selected; the first non-deref-matching candidate in scan order still wins. The deref-only candidate is used as a fallback only if the whole candidate scan finds no non-deref match. This mirrors Rust's autoderef order: exact/autoref matches at the current deref level are preferred over stepping to a further deref level.

rules.title: Once a by-value-self deref-fallback candidate is chosen, the receiver is materialized via an explicit deref
rules.statement: When the selected method candidate is the deref-fallback (by-value `self`, receiver was `&T`/`&mut T`/`*T`), the receiver expression is replaced with an explicit deref of the pointee before building the call. Soundness of the resulting move/copy is enforced by borrow-checking downstream, not by this dispatch step.
